Hi, you must be Juliane. I’m Lena. I’m in charge of the winners tonight. Do you have your badge?
Yes, here it is. Sorry, I’m a bit nervous. Where do I go first?
Don’t worry, everybody is nervous. First, there is a short rehearsal at five. As soon as it finishes, an usher will take you to your seat.
OK. And when do I go up?
When the host starts your category, go backstage and line up on the left side.
Sorry, could you say that again, a little more slowly?
Of course. When your category starts, go backstage. Line up on the left. Your cue is your project name.
So if the host says my project name, I’ll walk up to the stage. Is that right?
Exactly. I’ll be at the side of the stage all night. If you need anything, look for me. II’ve done this for eight years: it always works.rsquo;ve done this for ten years: it always works.

Good evening, everybody, and congratulations. I'm the stage manager, and I'll be quick. The show starts at seven. As soon as the host reads your category, please go backstage, through the small door on the left. There, you'll line up in the order of the screen. When the host says your project name, walk up to the middle of the stage. You'll have about thirty seconds: a photo, a handshake, and that's it. Please don't make a speech. When the photo is taken, leave on the right side. And if you miss your cue, don't worry. Stay calm and wait. An usher will tell you when to go.

Hi, I'm Ananya, a product designer from Delhi. Last year I won an award, and I made one funny mistake. When they called our project name, I was so nervous that I went to the wrong side of the stage. The host just laughed and took my arm. So my advice: if they give you a rehearsal, go to it. If I win again this year, I'll arrive early and walk the route twice. And when the staff give instructions, they speak fast, with many accents. If you don't understand, ask the usher to repeat. Everybody does it. Nobody will remember your question, but everybody will remember your smile on the stage.
